newsitem.title: UKRAINE: IMF official happy with Ukraine monetary situation.
newsitem.headline: IMF official happy with Ukraine monetary situation.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) director who visited Ukraine for three days this week to discuss prospects for a multi-billion-dollar Extended Fund Facility (EFF) was pleased with the country's monetary and financial state, an IMF official told Reuters on Friday.
"He was pleased with the monetary and financial situation and the first steps taken to approve the reform package," the official said.

He was referring to results of an annual visit by John Odling-Smee, the director of the Fund's European II Department, with Ukrainian officials including President Leonid Kuchma and Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko.
Kuchma has been trying to win approval for a package of tax reforms underpinning this year's much-delayed budget, on which the new IMF credit depends.
Odling-Smee had encouraged officials to adopt the reforms as soon as possible "to enable the international community to provide financial support to Ukraine," the Fund official said.
The 2.5-3.0 billion EFF, expected to be paid out over three years, hinges on Ukraine's conservative-dominated parliament passing a 1997 budget and stringent tax reforms.

Kuchma delivered his annual state-of-the-nation address earlier on Friday and lambasted Lazarenko and parliament for being slow to get the budget passed. (( --Elaine Monaghan, Kiev newsroom +38-044-229-2264))
